resources.string: Next time the app will open straight on the tools.
Material You, takes the palette from the wallpaper
Kotlin Multiplatform · Compose Multiplatform · Material 3 Expressive

A free multitool: network, converters, calculators, text, developer and device utilities. Everything runs locally where possible. Tools that need a system API are marked with the platforms they support.
Try another query, or clear the category filter.
The link points at a tool that does not exist. It may have been renamed.
Columns keep one line, the table scrolls sideways
The CV is not filled in yet. It lives in resume.json next to the app data.
Your browser does not support this feature
Exact age from the date and time of birth. Years, months and days, total months, weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds lived, weekday of birth and a live countdown to the next birthday.
Date of birth is after the reference date
Aspect ratios, px ↔ dp ↔ sp and PPI. Simplify a ratio, match it to common formats, scale sizes proportionally, get PPI from resolution and diagonal.
Battery runtime, charging time and mAh ↔ Wh. Runtime under a load in mA or W, charging time from charger current, conversion at a given voltage.
BMI, BMR, daily calories, ideal weight and body fat. BMI with WHO category, BMR by Mifflin-St Jeor, calories by activity, ideal weight by four formulas, US Navy body fat.
Waist must be larger than neck
Expressions with parentheses, powers and functions. Trigonometry, logarithms, factorials and constants. The last 10 results are kept.
Growth of a deposit or investment, year by year. A chosen compounding period and monthly top-ups.
Price after discounts, VAT added or extracted. One or two discounts, VAT on top of a net price or taken out of a gross one, 20% by default.
Fuel needed and the cost of a trip. From distance, consumption (L/100 km, km/L or mpg) and price, split between passengers.
Series resistor for one or more LEDs. Exact value, nearest E12/E24, actual current and the power rating required.
Supply voltage must exceed the total forward voltage of the LEDs
Monthly payment, total interest and a full schedule. Annuity or differentiated payments.
Voltage, current, resistance and power from any two. SI prefixes like 4.7k, 100m and 22u are accepted.
Fill exactly two fields, leave the other two empty
Check the values: use numbers with optional SI prefix
Percent of a number, share and percent change. Plus adding or subtracting a percent.
BIN, OCT, DEC and HEX with bitwise operations. 8 to 64-bit two's complement words, shifts, rotations and a tappable bit row.
Resistor bands to value and back. 4, 5 and 6 bands: colors to value with tolerance and temperature coefficient, and value to colors.
Value cannot be shown with standard bands (0.1 Ω to 99 GΩ)
Tip, total and the share per person. Optionally rounded up to whole units.
Round each share up to a whole number
Output of an R1/R2 divider, or the resistor for a target. With current, power and the nearest E24 value.
Vout must be lower than Vin
AWG ↔ mm² ↔ diameter with resistance and ampacity. Copper resistance per km, current limits for chassis wiring and power transmission.
Clothing and shoe sizes across RU, EU, US and UK. International sizes for men's and women's clothing, shoe sizes with foot length in cm.
Cups, spoons, millilitres and grams for common ingredients. Oven temperature in °C, °F and gas marks.
160+ currencies with daily rates. Rates come from open.er-api.com, are cached for 12 hours and work offline.
Bits, bytes and download time. Decimal (kB, MB) and binary (KiB, MiB) prefixes, plus transfer time at a given speed.
Any base from 2 to 36, numbers of any length. Binary, octal, decimal and hex side by side.
Numbers and money amounts spelled out. English and Russian, up to quadrillions, in rubles and dollars.
Enter a number with up to 18 integer digits
Arabic to Roman and back, 1 to 3999. With a strict check of the notation.
Only 1 to 3999 can be written in Roman numerals
Fourteen kinds of units, from length to frequency. Length, mass, temperature, area, volume, speed, pressure, energy, power, data, time, angle, fuel economy, frequency.
Barcodes in seven formats with validation. EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, Code 128, Code 39, ITF and Codabar, each checked for its format, with a computed check digit.
HEX, rgb(), hsl(), hsv(), cmyk() and CSS names, any way round. Square or wheel palette, channel sliders, optional alpha and ready values for Compose and Android.
Alpha channel in HEX, rgba(), hsla() and Compose values
Color harmonies from one base color. Complementary, analogous, triadic, tetradic, split-complementary, tints, shades and a tonal ramp. Tap a swatch to copy its HEX.
WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio for text on a background. AA/AAA verdicts for normal and large text and the nearest passing color.
No lightness of this hue reaches 4.5:1 on this background.
Normal body text at 14 sp for reading long paragraphs.
px, rem, em, pt and percent, plus dp to px. Against an editable root and parent size, dp at Android densities.
Enter numbers. Root and parent sizes must be greater than zero.
Gradient preview with ready CSS and Compose Brush code. Two to four stops, an angle, linear or radial.
A full Material 3 color scheme from a seed. Every role as a swatch, palette styles, export to Kotlin and CSS variables.
QR codes for text, links, Wi-Fi, contacts and more. Email, phone, SMS, coordinates and Telegram, with colors, rounded modules and error correction level.
Every Material 3 text style on your own sample. Size, line height and weight, plus a modular scale calculator.
Base size must be greater than zero.
Base64 and hex, encode and decode. Standard or URL-safe Base64, with or without padding. Binary data is shown as a hex dump.
Not valid UTF-8, showing a hex dump.
File permissions as checkboxes, octal and symbolic notation. setuid, setgid and sticky bits, conversion both ways and a ready chmod command.
A cron expression explained in plain words. The next 5 run times of a 5-field expression, plus presets for common schedules.
Expression: minute hour day month weekday
No run in the next 30 years.
CSV or TSV to JSON or Markdown, and JSON back to CSV. Delimiter and quoted fields are detected automatically.
Expected a JSON array at the top level.
The array must contain objects only.
MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, CRC32 and HMAC. Of text or hex bytes, with hex or Base64 output.
Searchable reference of 1xx–5xx status codes with short explanations.
Search by code, name or description
Request headers accepted, the client may send the body.
Server switches to the protocol requested in Upgrade (e.g. WebSocket).
WebDAV: the request is being processed, no response yet.
Preliminary headers (usually Link for preloading) before the final response.
A new resource was created. Its URI is usually in Location.
Accepted for processing, but not completed yet.
Response was modified by a proxy.
Success, no body in the response.
Success. The client should reset the document view (form).
Part of the resource as requested by Range.
WebDAV: multiple status codes for multiple resources in the body.
WebDAV: members of a binding were already listed.
Delta encoding: response is a diff against a previous version.
Several representations available. The client chooses.
Resource moved permanently to the URI in Location. The method may change to GET.
Temporary redirect. Browsers usually switch to GET.
Fetch the result at another URI with GET (typical after POST).
Cached version is still valid (If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since).
Deprecated: the resource must be accessed through a proxy.
Temporary redirect keeping the method and body.
Permanent redirect keeping the method and body.
Malformed request syntax or invalid parameters.
Reserved. Some APIs use it for billing limits.
Authenticated but not allowed to access the resource.
HTTP method not supported for this resource (see Allow).
No representation matches the Accept headers.
Server timed out waiting for the request.
Conflict with the current state of the resource (e.g. version mismatch).
Resource permanently removed, no forwarding address.
A precondition header (If-Match etc.) evaluated to false.
Request body exceeds the server limit.
Request URI is longer than the server accepts.
Request body format is not supported.
Requested Range is outside the resource size.
Expect header requirement cannot be met.
Request was sent to a server that cannot produce a response for it.
Syntax is fine but semantic validation failed.
Server refuses to process a request that might be replayed (0-RTT).
Client must switch to another protocol (Upgrade).
Blocked for legal reasons (censorship, court order).
Server does not support the request method.
Gateway or proxy got an invalid response from the upstream.
Server is overloaded or down for maintenance. See Retry-After.
Gateway did not get a timely response from the upstream.
HTTP version in the request is not supported.
Content negotiation configuration error on the server.
WebDAV: not enough storage to complete the request.
WebDAV: infinite loop detected while processing.
Further extensions to the request are required.
Validate, format, minify and browse JSON. Indent with 2 or 4 spaces, sort keys, view as a collapsible tree, see structure stats, escape and unescape strings.
The input is larger than 8 MB. Split the document or use a desktop editor.
The input field is hidden: editing a document this large freezes the interface. Clear it to paste another one.
Not a valid escaped JSON string.
Header, payload and claims of a JWT. Standard claims explained, issue and expiry dates, validity. The signature is not verified.
The signature is not verified here: a well-formed token can still be forged or revoked.
Key events as you press them. Click the field and type: the last events with key name, code, modifiers and event type.
Markdown rendered as you type. Headings, bold and italic, inline code, lists, links, code blocks, blockquotes and rules.
Media type by file extension and back. Look up extensions by type or description.
Address with a domain of at least two letters.
http or https link up to the first whitespace.
Six hex pairs separated by : or -.
Year-month-day, month and day are range checked.
Day, month and four-digit year with dots.
+7 or 8 with optional brackets, spaces and dashes.
Country code and groups of digits in E.164 style.
Six or three hex digits after #.
Three Base64url parts, header starts with eyJ.
Name with any number of levels and a letter-only zone.
Starts with a letter, 3 to 20 characters.
At least 8 characters with lower and upper case, a digit and a symbol.
Fractional part after a dot or a comma.
Four digits of the series and six of the number.
A regex assembled from blocks. Quantifiers and flags, a test on a sample right away, or a ready pattern from the library.
start / end of text (of line with multiline)
one of / none of the characters
exactly n / at least n / from n to m
back-reference in pattern / group in replacement
Matches, groups and replacement preview for a regex. Positions, highlighted text, flags and a syntax cheat sheet.
Parse, compare and bump semantic versions. Pre-release rules, range checks (^ ~ >= < || x), bump major, minor, patch or pre-release.
Not a semantic version: expected MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
Escape and unescape strings for nine targets. JSON, Java/Kotlin, C, JavaScript, HTML, XML, shell, SQL and URI.
Percent-encoding, URL parsing and a query builder. Scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment, IDN hosts to punycode.
Off: keep URL delimiters, encode only unsafe characters
Random v4 and time-ordered v7 UUIDs, up to 100 at once. Parse any UUID: version, variant, embedded timestamp.
Not a UUID: expected 32 hex digits, optionally with dashes or braces.
OS, model, hardware and network of this device. Locale, time zone, screen, sensors and network interfaces on one screen.
No sensors are exposed on this platform.
Charge level, state, temperature, voltage and current. Health and cycle count where the platform exposes them.
No battery information is available on this device or browser.
Window size in px and dp, density and refresh rate. Font scale, physical DPI and HDR support.
What is in the clipboard, as text and hex. Length, line count and a hex preview. Clear it with one tap.
Solid colors and gradients to find dead pixels. Backlight bleed and banding too. Tap to cycle, long press to exit.
Opens a full-screen view. Tap anywhere for the next fill, long press to close.
Tap: next fill · Long press or ✕: exit
The screen as a lamp, with color and brightness. On Android also toggles the camera flash.
Every touch with its coordinates and pressure. Paint to find dead zones on the touchscreen.
Short, long and pattern vibrations. Checks the motor and haptics.
A random pick from your own list of options. Spinning animation and a history of results.
d4 to d100, coin flip and a history of rolls. Notation like 2d6+3.
Use NdM with optional modifiers, e.g. 2d6+3.
Days, hours and minutes left to your events, or elapsed since them. The list is saved on the device.
Enter a date as YYYY-MM-DD and a time as HH:MM.
One persistent note for quick text. With character, word and line counts.
Who owes whom after a shared purchase or trip. Equal shares, balances and the minimal list of transfers to settle up.
When to go to bed, or when to get up. 90-minute cycles plus 14 minutes to fall asleep.
A cycle lasts about 90 minutes, falling asleep takes about 14. Five or six cycles make a full night.
Several named counters with plus, minus and reset. Values are kept between launches.
Up to five products compared by price per unit. Per kilogram, litre or piece. The cheapest is highlighted with the overpay of the others.
Daily water estimate from weight, activity and climate. In millilitres and glasses.
Enter a weight between 20 and 300 kg.
Estimate: 33 ml per kg plus 350–700 ml for exercise and 500 ml in hot weather. Not medical advice.
Below the healthy band, check the measurement
Above the natural ceiling for most people
Waist ratios, body surface area, lean mass and FFMI. Waist-to-height and waist-to-hip, lean mass by three formulas. BMI, BMR and TDEE live in the BMI and body calculator.
Used for FFMI when filled in.
All measurements must be positive, body fat below 70 %.
Waist to height under 0.5 is the simplest single marker of central fat. The waist to hip ratio adds fat distribution on top of it.
BSA is what drug and infusion dosages are scaled by. Mosteller is the one used at the bedside because it is a single square root.
Boer is the general-purpose one, James overestimates in heavy lifters, Hume was fitted on a hospital population.
Normalization scales FFMI to a height of 1.8 m so tall and short people can be compared. Without a measured body fat percentage the number is only as good as the Boer estimate.
Kilocalories by activity or by heart rate. A MET table of about fifty activities, or an average heart rate by the Keytel formula.
Weight and duration must be greater than zero.
Keytel formula, needs sex and age.
Warm-up, cool-down, easy movement between hard days
Fat oxidation and capillary growth, the bulk of endurance volume
Lactate threshold, race pace for 10K to half marathon
VO2max intervals, only in short bouts
Max heart rate and five training zones. Max HR by three age formulas or measured, zones by %HRmax and by Karvonen reserve.
From a ramp test or a race finish.
Max HR must be above the resting HR.
1RM from a working set by six formulas. Their average and a table of training weights from 50 to 100 %.
Weight above zero, reps from 1 to 30.
Above 12 reps every formula drifts: use a set of 3–8 for a usable estimate.
Distance, time and pace: any two give the third. Splits, speed and Riegel race predictions from 5K to marathon.
Enter a positive distance and time as mm:ss or h:mm:ss.
On a treadmill 1 % incline roughly matches the air resistance of running outdoors. Above 12 km/h the correction grows, and the belt reads distance from the roller, not from you.
Calories and macros from your TDEE and goal. Protein and fat per kilogram, carbs as the remainder, split over 3 to 6 meals.
Take it from the bmi-body tool.
Check the values: shift within ±60 %, protein up to 5 g/kg, fat up to 4 g/kg.
Protein and fat alone exceed the calorie target: lower them or raise the calories.
Water is not part of this: the water-intake tool in the everyday category already works it out from weight, activity and air temperature.
Named training plans with sets, reps, weight and rest. Estimated length, total volume, JSON export and import.
No plans yet. Create one and add exercises to it.
This is not a plan exported from here.
Runs a workout plan or a plain HIIT/Tabata. Work and rest countdown, auto-advance, sound and vibration.
No saved plans: create one in the workout builder or switch to intervals.
Nothing to run: check work time, rounds and sets.
Magnetic heading with a rotating dial. From the orientation sensor, plus pitch and roll.
Keep the device level and away from magnets. Wave it in a figure eight to calibrate.
Two-axis spirit level and inclinometer. From the accelerometer: pitch and roll in degrees.
Coordinates, altitude, speed and distance travelled. Several coordinate formats, accuracy, km/h with maximum, bearing and a map link.
Location access is needed to read GPS.
Live X/Y/Z acceleration and a vibration meter. Magnitude and peak, for engines, fans and washing machines.
Magnetic field in µT per axis, with a live chart. A rising value near an object means ferrous metal or a magnet.
Earth's field is 25–65 µT. Bring the top of the phone close to the object.
Illuminance in lux from the light sensor. Reference levels and an EV value.
Pressure in hPa and mmHg, trend and barometric altitude. Altitude relative to a sea-level reference you can set.
Steps since the app opened, distance and calories. From the hardware step counter, your stride length and weight.
Step counting needs the activity recognition permission.
On-screen ruler in centimetres and inches. Across the screen or along it. Calibrate against a real object or enter the screen diagonal. Full screen turns it vertical and gives it the whole display.
Match the outline to a real object or enter the screen diagonal
The system often reports a rounded DPI. Enter the panel resolution and its diagonal and the scale is computed from them.
An angle measured on screen. Drag two arms around the centre and read the angle between them.
This device has no such sensor.
The browser needs permission to read motion sensors. Tap to allow.
Approximate loudness in dB from the microphone. Live chart, min/avg/max and reference levels. Uncalibrated: compare, do not certify.
Motorcycle, power tools: hearing risk over 8 h
Sine tone from 20 Hz to 20 kHz for speaker and hearing tests, note presets, adjustable duration.
Above 16 kHz most adults hear nothing, and that is normal.
Click track from 30 to 300 BPM with tap tempo. Accented first beat and 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8 time.
Devices and services on the local network. Found via SSDP (UPnP) and multicast DNS (Bonjour / DNS-SD).
DNS records of any type over DoH, UDP or your own resolver. A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, SRV, CAA, PTR and more. DNS-over-HTTPS works everywhere, and answers can be compared across resolvers.
Browser build: only DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers are available, including your own below.
Resolvers return different answers (propagation in progress or GeoDNS).
JSON API (?name=…) and RFC 8484 wire format (?dns=…) are both supported. Auto tries JSON first and remembers what worked.
Same filtering plus EDNS Client Subnet

HTTP requests with headers, body, auth and history. GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS, query editor, raw or form body, Bearer and Basic auth, response headers and cookies, saved requests and curl.
In the browser only CORS-safelisted response headers are visible, the rest are hidden by the browser itself.
The browser follows redirects on its own, the switch has no effect on the web.
GET and HEAD are sent without a body.
No URL found in the command.
Public IP, geolocation, ISP and ASN. For your connection or any address, with its time zone.
IP address or hostname (empty = my IP)
Live hosts in your subnet with names and open ports. Ping and TCP probes, resolved names and common ports.
Enter a subnet of /20 or smaller
Vendor by MAC address, formats and address bits. OUI lookup, format conversion, unicast/multicast and local/universal bits, random MAC generator.
The browser has no sockets: this works in the Android, iOS and desktop apps.
In the browser, requests are limited by CORS: the target server must allow cross-origin access.
Interfaces with addresses, MAC, MTU and state. IPv4 and IPv6, plus Wi-Fi details on Android (SSID, BSSID, RSSI, link speed, DNS, gateway).
SSID and BSSID require the location permission.
Reply times and packet loss over ICMP, TCP or HTTP. min/avg/max/jitter and a live chart. The browser only has the HTTP mode.
ICMP is not available here: TCP ping measures a connect to the port, HTTP ping measures a HEAD request round trip.
HTTP ping measures a HEAD request round trip.
TCP connect scan of a host with service names. A list, ranges or the top common ports.
Well-known TCP/UDP ports with their services. Searchable by number or name.
Public resolvers and their response times. IPv4, IPv6, DoH, DoT and filtering, with a benchmark.
Fast, privacy-focused. 1.1.1.2 blocks malware, 1.1.1.3 also adult content
Blocks ads and trackers. 94.140.14.140 is unfiltered
EU public resolver, protective variants available
Measured in the app over the probes issued by yandex.ru/internet. In the browser it may be blocked by CORS.
Download only: the file must be at least 25 MB.
The measurement runs on the provider's page, the app only opens it.
Latency, download and upload speed. Against Cloudflare, Yandex, your own OpenSpeedTest server or any large file.
The address returns a web page, not a data stream. If the server is behind a login, open the test paths without it.
Results depend on the chosen source, the route to it and your device.
IPv4 and IPv6 subnets: network, broadcast and host range. Mask, wildcard, binary form and address type.
Split a network into subnets, VLSM and CIDR summaries. Equal subnets, VLSM by required hosts, summarized CIDR blocks, IP ranges to CIDR.
Enter a network and a count
Too many subnets for this prefix
Enter a network and host counts
The network is too small for these hosts
Certificate chain, protocol and cipher of a host. SANs, validity and fingerprints.
Path to a host hop by hop with reply times. Reverse DNS names, ICMP echo with increasing TTL.
A magic packet to wake a computer. With a list of saved devices.
Registration data for domains, IP blocks and AS numbers. RDAP works everywhere, classic whois on port 43 where sockets are available.
Domain, IP address, network or AS number
Grams, metres and cm³ of filament, and what is left on a spool. For a material and diameter, the remainder from a measured weight.
The spool alone weighs more than the measurement.
Extruder calibration: E-steps, flow and volumetric limit. New E-steps from a 100 mm test, extrusion multiplier from a measured wall.
All three values must be greater than zero.
The extruder pushed more than asked, so the new value is lower.
A correction over 15 % usually means wrong E-steps or a wrong filament diameter, not flow.
All four values must be greater than zero.
The hotend cannot melt this much: drop the speed or the layer height.
Marlin and Klipper commands with parameters. What each one actually does, searchable by code or by wording.
Linear move. G0 travel, G1 print. E is the extruder position, F the feedrate in mm/min.
Clockwise / counter-clockwise arc move, either by centre offset I J or by radius R.
Dwell: pause for P milliseconds or S seconds.
Firmware retract and recover using the M207/M208 settings.
Home the listed axes. With no arguments homes all of them.
Run bed levelling and build the mesh (ABL / UBL, depends on the build).
Absolute / relative positioning for all axes.
Set the current position without moving. G92 E0 resets the extruder counter.
Enable / disable stepper drivers on the listed axes.
Absolute / relative extrusion mode for the E axis.
Disable steppers. S sets the idle timeout in seconds.
Set steps per millimetre for each axis. Store with M500.
Set the hotend temperature and continue without waiting.
Report current hotend and bed temperatures.
Part cooling fan on with speed S (0–255) / fan off.
Set the hotend temperature and wait: S waits on heating only, R also on cooling.
Emergency stop: shuts down heaters and motors immediately.
Show a message on the printer display.
Set the bed temperature without waiting.
Set the bed temperature and wait for it.
Maximum acceleration per axis / print and travel acceleration.
Maximum feedrate per axis in mm/s.
Jerk per axis, or junction deviation with J.
Beep at frequency S for P milliseconds.
PID autotune: E0 hotend, E-1 bed, S target, C cycles, U applies the result.
Save settings to EEPROM / load them / reset to firmware defaults.
Print the current settings as G-code.
Filament change: park, unload and wait for the new filament.
IDEX mode: full control, duplication or mirrored duplication.
Z probe offset relative to the nozzle. Negative values move the nozzle closer.
Linear Advance factor K, the Marlin equivalent of pressure advance.
Set pressure advance for the active extruder without restarting.
Probe the bed and build a mesh. SAVE_CONFIG stores it.
Load, save or delete a stored bed mesh profile.
Interactive probe Z offset calibration using the paper test.
Measure the bed corners and report how far to turn each levelling screw.
Level a four-motor gantry (Voron-style) by probing the corners.
Level the bed with independent Z motors.
Sweep a parameter over Z height, the standard way to tune pressure advance.
Temporarily override speed, acceleration and corner velocity.
Set any heater by name, including a chamber heater.
Restart the firmware and clear a shutdown state.
Write the values calibration produced into printer.cfg and restart.
Pause, resume or cancel the current print (macros from the standard config).
Layer height and extrusion width for a nozzle. 25–75 % limits, first layer, layer count for a target height.
Nozzle and layer must be greater than zero.
Cost of an FDM part and a suggested price. Filament, electricity, failed prints and markup, cost per gram and total.
Fill in the fields: failure rate below 100 %, all values positive.
Rough FDM print time from the model and settings. Volume, layer height, extrusion width, speed, infill and wall count. Not a slicer.
A rough estimate, typically within ±30 % of the slicer: travel moves, retractions and acceleration are folded into one efficiency factor.
Check the values: infill 0–100 %, at least one wall.
Cost of an MSLA print. Resin with support waste, IPA, gloves and electricity for the print time.
For MSLA (LCD) printers: the resin volume comes from the slicer, supports and the raft are added as waste.
Fill in every field with non-negative numbers.
Scale factor for shrinkage and X/Y/Z steps correction. From a printed calibration cube.
Fill in every measurement and the current steps per mm.
An error above 2 % is mechanical: check belts, pulley grub screws and the extrusion multiplier before touching the steps.
Segment plan for a temperature tower. Material presets and the M104/M109 lines for the layer-change script.
Check the values: 2–30 segments, non-zero step.
Two hashes compared, algorithm detected by length. Case, spaces and separators are ignored, and the first differing character is pointed out.
One of the values contains non-hex characters.
The lengths differ, so these are different algorithms or a truncated value.
Random passwords or passphrases with entropy and crack time. Cryptographically random, selectable character sets, English and Russian word lists.
At least one from each set
Select at least one character set.
Length is smaller than the number of selected sets.
Entropy estimate and crack time for a password. Penalties for sequences, repeats, keyboard walks, dates and dictionary words, with suggestions. Nothing leaves the device.
The password is analysed on this device and is never sent anywhere.
A password checked against the Have I Been Pwned corpus. k-anonymity: only the first 5 characters of its SHA-1 hash leave the device.
Absence from the corpus does not make a weak password safe. Check its strength as well.

The password is hashed with SHA-1 on the device. Only the first 5 hex characters of the hash are sent to the API, which returns every hash suffix sharing that prefix, usually several hundred. The match is found locally, so the service never learns which password was checked.
Random numbers, draws, dice, coins, picks and bytes. Cryptographically random, unique draws, notation like 3d6+2, shuffling a list, hex or Base64 bytes.
Enter a valid range and count.
The range is smaller than the requested count.
Enter a size from 1 to 1024 bytes.
RFC 6238 one-time codes from a secret or otpauth:// URI. Base32 secret, with the remaining validity of the current code shown.
Not a valid Base32 secret (letters A–Z and digits 2–7).
Characters 0–127 with decimal, hex, octal and binary codes. Search by character, code or name.
Search: character, decimal, hex or name
UPPER, lower, Title, Sentence, camelCase and more. PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and Cyrillic is handled.
Caesar, ROT13, ROT47, Atbash, Vigenère and reverse. Caesar with brute force, Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.
Find and replace with a match count. Case-insensitive, whole-word or regular-expression matching.
Text typed in the wrong layout, repaired. ЙЦУКЕН ↔ QWERTY both ways with punctuation, ё and the shifted digit row. The direction is detected automatically.
Russian written in Latin letters (privet → привет) is a different job: that is the Transliteration tool.
Sort, dedupe, reverse, shuffle and number lines. Trim, add prefix/suffix, join or split by a separator.
Placeholder text in Latin or Russian. By paragraphs, sentences or words.
Text ↔ Morse with audio playback. Latin and Cyrillic letters, digits and punctuation.
Whitespace, HTML, diacritics and emoji cleaned out. Collapse spaces, trim, remove line breaks and non-printable characters, normalize quotes and dashes.
Characters, words, sentences, paragraphs and bytes. Reading and speaking time, most frequent words.
Two texts compared line by line. Added and removed lines highlighted, with a similarity score.
Russian ↔ Latin by passport, GOST or readable scheme. ICAO, GOST 7.79-2000, plus URL slug generation.
Code point, bytes, category and block of every character. UTF-8 and UTF-16 bytes, \\u, HTML and URL escapes, lookup by code point.
Month view with ISO week numbers, starting on Monday. Tap a day for its weekday, week, day of year and distance from today.
Countdown with presets and a sound at the end. Pomodoro mode switches work and break automatically.
Enter a duration greater than zero.
Difference between dates, periods added or subtracted. Weekday, ISO week, day of year and other facts about a date.
Millisecond stopwatch with laps. Lap time and total time for each split.
Sunrise, sunset, solar noon and twilight for a place and date. Day length, then civil, nautical and astronomical twilight by the NOAA algorithm.
Offset must be between -14 and 14 hours.
Epoch time to date and back, local and UTC. Seconds, ms, µs and ns are detected automatically, and the current epoch time is shown.
Shifts with breaks summed up, with pay. Total in hours and minutes, decimal hours and pay at an hourly rate.
Check the times: HH:MM, break in whole minutes.
Time in several zones and a converter between them. Offsets against your local time, and a given time converted between zones.
Right here, no PDF and no external link
The tool needs a system API the browser does not expose. The desktop, Android and iOS apps have it.

Android and Kotlin Multiplatform developer, systems and network engineer. This app is a set of offline tools: network, converters, text, developer, sensors. The About me tab has my projects, articles and CV.
Whetstone, Linpack and SciMark 2.0 on this device. Ported from the public reference sources, plus SHA-256, memory copy and Mandelbrot throughput.
Floating point, trigonometry and branches. Curnow and Wichmann, 1976, ported from the netlib C source with the reference module weights.
Dense 500x500 system solved by Gaussian elimination. Scored over the reference operation count 2n^3/3 + 2n^2.
Five NIST kernels: FFT, SOR, Monte Carlo, sparse matrix multiply and LU. The composite is their mean, as in the original driver.
Hashing throughput on a 1 MiB block. Not a standard benchmark, compare only with other runs of this app.
Sequential copy of a 16 MiB array, counting both the read and the write. Not a standard benchmark.
Escape-time iteration over a fixed 256x256 window: integer-heavy with unpredictable branches. Not a standard benchmark.
The score measures the runtime as much as the processor: the same device gives different numbers in the app and in a browser. Compare like with like.
Sustained load with throughput and temperature charts. A timer stops the run on its own.
The browser runs everything on one thread, so the load here is single-threaded and the page stays responsive between work units. Temperature is not available to a web page on any platform.
Threads to load. Fewer threads heat the chip less but also show throttling later.
The run stops itself after this long. With the timer off it runs until you stop it or leave the tool.
This platform does not report temperature to an ordinary app, so only throughput is charted.
A reading classified by ACC/AHA 2017 and ESC/ESH. The two guidelines disagree, and pulse and mean arterial pressure are added.
Diastolic has to be below systolic.
A single reading classifies nothing on its own: guidelines call for an average of readings taken on separate days, seated, after five minutes of rest.
HbA1c in DCCT percent, IFCC mmol/mol and average glucose. Conversion by the ADAG regression.
That converts to an HbA1c outside 0 to 25 %.
The ADAG regression came from 507 participants and describes a group, not a person: individual average glucose scatters around these numbers by a wide margin.
VO2 max from a Cooper test, Rockport walk or heart rates. Maximal oxygen uptake by the 12-minute run, the one-mile walk or the max-to-resting ratio.
The inputs give a result outside any plausible range.
Field tests estimate to within roughly 10 to 15 % of a laboratory measurement, and only when the effort was genuinely maximal.
Check the values: weight and time above zero, age 10 to 100, heart rate 40 to 240.
How much caffeine is still in you, and when it drops. From a dose after a given time, down to the level you want before sleep.
Dose, half-life and threshold all have to be above zero.
Half-life runs from about 3 to 7 hours in healthy adults and shifts with oral contraceptives, pregnancy, smoking and liver enzyme variants.
Blood alcohol estimate and time to clear. Widmark formula, with the spread the formula actually carries.
Check the values: volume, strength, weight and time.

An estimate, not a measurement. The distribution factor and elimination rate vary by more than the numbers above, and food, medication and illness shift both. Never use this to decide whether to drive.
A continuous tone that stays on until you stop it. Sine, square, triangle, sawtooth or noise, from 1 Hz up to the Nyquist limit of the audio output.
The ceiling is %d Hz: half the sample rate the audio output opened at. Nothing above that can be reproduced, and a speaker or headphone will roll off long before it.
Live spectrum from the microphone with peak and note. The harmonics above the peak and total harmonic distortion.
Microphone access is asked for when you start.
Too quiet to pick a peak out of the noise floor.
A larger window resolves closer frequencies but reacts more slowly, a smaller one is the other way round. Distortion measured this way includes whatever the microphone itself adds.
Microphone access was refused. Allow it in the browser or system settings and start again.
The microphone is busy in another application.

How many samples go into one transform. A larger window separates frequencies that sit close together but reacts more slowly, because it has to collect more sound first. A smaller one is the other way round. At 48 kHz: 1024 gives 47 Hz per bin and reacts in 21 ms, 8192 gives 6 Hz per bin and reacts in 171 ms.
